ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (UIAF); Ley 2010 de 2019 (beneficial owner reporting); Decreto Único Reglamentario 2555 de 2010; Resolución DIAN 000164 de 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUBF); Código de Comercio arts. 98-130

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original Certificate of Incorporation and Existence of Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registry / Ministry of Commerce of the shareholder's jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for the Local Legal Representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the shareholder's jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Passport Copies and Certified Address Affidavit of Ultimate Beneficial Owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or Consular Officer of the UBO's nationality/residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs and counterparties against the Colombian UIAF terrorist financing list, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, and the Colombian consolidated PEP list maintained by UIAF. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs and for transactions involving high-risk jurisdictions. Ongoing transaction monitoring is mandatory under the SAGRILAFT system for money laundering and terrorist financing risk management.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cámara de Comercio - Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) / Sistema Integral de Información Registral (SII)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Spanish or in Latin-script transliteration. Non-Spanish terms are subject to phonetic transliteration. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, nor cause confusion as to the nature of the entity. The suffix 'S.A.S.' must be used where applicable.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name reservation is rejected, submit a written administrative appeal to the 'Delegado Registral' of the same Chamber of Commerce within 10 business days of the rejection notice, attaching a list of alternative proposed names and legal arguments. The appeal will be resolved administratively; a further adverse decision may be challenged before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio through the jurisdictional administrative process.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is generally not accepted as the sole registered office of a commercial SAS. A physical address within the elected municipal domicile is mandatory. Shared administrative space or a registered agent's physical office may satisfy the requirement provided the company can receive judicial notices and official correspondence at that location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate (estimated 5% annual probability). Unannounced physical inspections may be conducted by the Cámara de Comercio or the DIAN if revenue levels or invoice patterns trigger verification protocols. For an import/distribution business without local warehousing, the likelihood is below average unless tax irregularities are suspected.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille of foreign corporate documents (3 sets)

Public deed of incorporation (por escritura pública) or private deed with legalization

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative processing fee and compliance filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for cross-border SAS incorporations; flat fee scope

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), regulated by Decree 1074 of 2015, Book 2, Title 2, Supplementing Commercial Code Articles 373-390
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (Bogotá Chamber of Commerce) acting as the delegated commercial registry under the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation document) registered through the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital; S.A.S. entities may be incorporated with zero subscribed and paid capital. Any subscribed unpaid capital must be paid within two years from incorporation. No escrow account is legally required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Founder-subscriber hereby subscribes and accepts all shares set out in the incorporation document, and the subscribed capital is approved for registration under the Chamber of Commerce rules. RESOLVED: That the registered office of the Company is established at [address] in Bogotá D.C., and the Manager is directed to complete the corresponding commercial registration. RESOLVED: That the following officers are appointed: [Name] as Manager and general legal representative, and [Name] as Secretary; their powers are as defined in the bylaws. RESOLVED: That the officers are instructed to obtain the RUT and all operating licenses and to take all actions necessary to commence lawful business. RESOLVED: That all prior acts performed by the founder for the company's formation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) online portal operated by the Cámara de Comercio
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the RUES system with the founder's electronic ID. Submit three preferred corporate names for evaluation, providing the basic activity code (ISIC 4631). The system will verify uniqueness against the national commercial registry. Once approved, the name is reserved for 30 days and may be extended.
required_dossiers: Electronic identification certificate of the founder
List of three proposed company names
Primary business activity description and proposed address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged as confusingly similar, resubmit alternative names through the same RUES portal within 5 business days; the system will indicate the specific conflicting registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Private Incorporation Document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founder before the Bogotá Chamber of Commerce or through a notary public for contributions of real estate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Documento Privado de Constitución containing the complete bylaws, share subscription, corporate purpose, officer appointments, registered office address, and duration. All subscribers must sign the document, evidencing acceptance of the share allocation. If any contribution consists of real estate, the document must be elevated to a public deed and recorded with the Deed and Property Registry.
required_dossiers: Valid national ID or passport of each subscriber
Name reservation certificate issued by RUES
Power of attorney if signature is delegated to a representative
Real estate title documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or registry identifies a formal defect, execute a corrective amendment or new private instrument and resubmit within 10 business days; the correction shall not retroactively invalidate the incorporation if filed before the commercial registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá through the RUES registry window or authorized online filing service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the fully executed incorporation document electronically via RUES, pay the commercial registration fee, and attach all required dossiers. The Chamber reviews the legality of the incorporation under Law 1258 of 2008, verifies officer eligibility, and issues the Commercial Registration Certificate (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal).
required_dossiers: Executed private incorporation document
Name reservation certificate
Registration fee settlement receipt
ID copies of all appointed officers and legal representative
Private-address consent or lease contract for the registered office, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a deficiency notice, cure the specified defect within 30 calendar days by filing an amending private document. Failure to cure within the statutory period voids the filing and requires a new submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) – National Tax and Customs Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: In the DIAN electronic portal, complete the mandatory pre-registration using the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation issued by the Chamber of Commerce. Request the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) with the appropriate responsibilities for the green coffee bean wholesale activity (ISIC 4631). The RUT will be activated within the statutory period after submission of accurate data.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Certificate (Estado de Existencia)
Legal representative identification document
RUT pre-registration confirmation number
Registered office address and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects the pre-registration due to data inconsistency, correct the data in the RUT portal and resubmit within 10 business days; no penalty applies when the correction is made before the first tax due date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating License and Zoning Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Gobierno – Alcaldía Mayor de Bogotá and, where applicable, the Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for the municipal operating license (Licencia de Funcionamiento) and the Certificado de Uso de Suelo (zoning certificate) at the local mayor's office or through the virtual window. Include the green coffee business activity and storage details. If the premises include warehousing, coordinate with the fire department for an inspection and obtain an environmental registration if required for low-impact agricultural product warehousing.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Tax Registration (RUT)
Copy of lease or ownership title for the business premises
Premises layout plan and safety signage description
Fire department inspection certificate, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the zoning certificate is denied because the activity is not allowed in the selected premises, relocate to a mixed-use or industrial zone and resubmit the application within 20 business days; administrative appeals may be filed within 5 business days of denial.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Desarrollo Económico and Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente – Alcaldía Mayor de Bogotá D.C.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificado de Uso de Suelo and Licencia de Funcionamiento (Municipal Operating and Zoning License) for Commercial Mercantile Activity

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) – under the Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / No Full EIA Report Required. A low-impact environmental registration may apply for warehousing and distribution operations involving bagged green coffee beans; activities limited to sorting and repacking without processing are Category III-light.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Decree 1076 of 2015 discharge limits for any washwater and wastewater; minimisation of dust emissions; use of sealed containers for green coffee; solid waste must be removed by licensed municipal collection services; COD/BOD limits per local regulations; no significant VOC emissions expected from unprocessed green coffee beans.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Oficina de Bomberos, structural load certification for storage racking systems, and a workplace risk assessment compliant with Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) under Law 1562 of 2012 and Decree 1072 of 2015.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — official tax and customs portal: https://www.dian.gov.co; transactional portal: Muisca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Colombian S.A.S. is constituted through a notarized public deed or private document, registered with the local Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio) to obtain the official certificate of existence and legal representation. The legal representative or a designated officer then obtains an NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) by completing and submitting Registration Form RUT (Registro Único Tributario) through the DIAN Muisca electronic system or at a DIAN service office. For non-resident shareholders, a local attorney-in-fact with power of attorney is required to sign the RUT filing. There is no minimum capital requirement for the S.A.S.; the NIT is issued immediately upon validation and remains the single statutory taxpayer ID for income tax, VAT, withholding, and customs operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: Colombian-resident SAS entities are taxed on worldwide income under the general corporate income tax regime; no pass-through or flow-through treatment is available. Gains and income are taxed at the entity level; dividends remitted abroad are subject to a separate withholding tax. Cross-border hybrid structures are subject to the statutory control rules and the OECD-aligned anti-hybrid provisions.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No 'check-the-box' or US-style entity classification election exists. The legal entity form determines tax status: an S.A.S. is always a corporation for income tax and VAT purposes. Optional regimes that may be elected when statutory requirements are met include: (i) the Simple Taxation Regime (Régimen Simple de Tributación – SIMPLE) for small taxpayers under defined turnover thresholds; (ii) special permanent establishment treatment under a Free Trade Zone license; (iii) the VAT non-responsible status only for qualifying natural persons, not for an S.A.S. exporting coffee; and (iv) preferential tax stabilization agreements for certain large investments. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available; Colombia applies Law 2277 of 2022 and Decree regulations implementing BEPS Action 2 anti-hybrid rules for cross-border payments and entity characterization.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general numeric obligatory registration threshold under Colombian VAT law. Any person or entity undertaking a taxable transaction, importing goods, commencing business activities, or holding itself out as a VAT responsible taxpayer must register in the RUT and obtain an NIT. The simplified 'no responsable' VAT status is limited to natural persons whose taxable activity does not involve imports or exports and whose annual gross turnover does not exceed 3,500 UVT (Tax Value Units) as annually adjusted. The Colombian S.A.S. distributing green coffee beans and exporting goods must therefore register and remain a full IVA responsible taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: DIAN mandates mandatory electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica de Venta) for all VAT responsible taxpayers, including SAS exporters. Invoices must be generated in XML format using DIAN-authorized billing software or a certified technological provider; the electronic invoice must include the mandatory fiscal identification elements, an assigned serial like CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica), and a QR code. The invoice XML is transmitted in real time to DIAN through its web services/API environment (Radian and Muisca platforms) for validation and 'prevalidation' before being delivered to the buyer. No physical fiscal stamping is applied; legal validity depends on successful DIAN rejection-free validation. Export invoices must reference the customs export declaration and may be issued with 0% IVA pursuant to statutory export rules.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods, including specialty green coffee beans, are zero-rated for IVA purposes under Colombian Law 2010 of 2019 and complementary regulations. Eligibility requires that (i) the goods are physically exported from Colombian customs territory; (ii) the seller is the exporter of record and the customs export declaration is accepted by DIAN; (iii) title, risk, and ownership pass to a non-resident buyer; (iv) the export proceeds are received through the authorized foreign exchange market in accordance with rules of the Banco de la República; and (v) the exporter maintains complete documentary evidence of the exit of goods from Colombia, the receipt of payment, and the identification of the foreign buyer. Offshoring of services to non-residents may also qualify as an export when the service is used abroad and the beneficiary is a non-resident, with specific requirements for declaration and supporting contracts.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) accepted and validated by DIAN customs authorities
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill proving physical departure from Colombian territory
Commercial invoice issued in accordance with DIAN electronic invoicing rules
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the intermediary financial institution evidencing conversion and repatriation of export proceeds
Certificate of Origin (where a preferential tariff is claimed) issued by the competent authority or chamber of commerce
Insurance and inland transport documentation evidencing the route to the port or airport
Veterinary/phytosanitary certificate or FNC-related coffee documentation if required for destination-market admission
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to strict DIAN audit scrutiny through cross-matching of electronic invoices, customs exit records, maritime/air transport manifests, and financial-system foreign exchange data. If export documentation is missing, false, or inconsistent, DIAN may reverse the zero-rated treatment, assess IVA plus interest, and impose penalties for inaccurate or false declarations. In the absence of good faith, the penalty can be equal to 100%–200% of the amount of output VAT omitted, and a false export VAT refund may be classified as an inexistent tax loss under Article 647 of the Tax Code, triggering a capitalization penalty and criminal liability for fraudulent VAT refund under Colombian criminal law. Additionally, repatriation beyond the 180-day term without authorized extension may trigger exchange-control sanctions under the foreign exchange regime and loss of zero-rating evidence evidence. Retrospective clawback extends to a period of five years from the filing date under DIAN's general statute of limitations, with extensions when the proceeding is formally opened.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (the Central Bank of Colombia) is the regulatory authority for foreign exchange and monetary policy. The foreign exchange regime is codified in Resolution 2023-01-001903 and complementary decrees, while the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) exercises customs, taxation, and foreign exchange-related enforcement. Authorized intermediaries (bancos comerciales, financiers, and brokers registered with Banco de la República) must channel all foreign exchange operations above the regulatory threshold.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is convertible for both current account and capital account transactions. Current account transactions (imports, exports, services, and remittances of profit) require no prior license or central bank authorization; however, they must be routed through an authorized intermediary (AIM) using the mandatory foreign exchange declaration (Declaración de Cambio, DCC) in accordance with Resolution 2023-01-001903. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment in an SAS and profit repatriation, are subject to mandatory registration with Banco de la República but are not subject to pre-approval. Net profit remittance requires audited financial statements, evidence that the foreign investment is duly registered, and proof that corporate and tax obligations are satisfied. No surrender or forced conversion is applied, but foreign exchange proceeds from exports must be channeled to the AIM within the legally prescribed term.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All merchandise export proceeds, including specialty green coffee beans, must be channeled exclusively through the official foreign exchange market. Colombian law requires exporters to receive and settle export proceeds within six (6) months from the date of the export bill of lading (or the date of the export declaration, as applicable), unless an extended term is approved by Banco de la República under a threshaded commercial financing schedule. The proceeds must be credited to a domestic account of the exporting SAS; the mandatory conversion requirement is functionally limited to the obligation to sell the foreign currency to an authorized intermediary or use it to pay obligations, with the equivalent COP calculated at the representative market rate (TRM). For coffee exports, the general six-month rule applies, subject to the contractual maturity of the documentary collection, LC, or pre-export financing facility.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Checking Account (Cuenta Corriente) for FX intermediation, import settlements, and FDI capital registration; no separate statutory capital escrow required
Operational Checking Account (Cuenta Corriente) / Trade Finance Working Line for Documentary Credits and foreign exchange transactions
Operational Checking Account (Cuenta Corriente) / Savings Account for FX collection and disbursement
Operational Checking Account (Cuenta Corriente) for permanent working capital and FX hedging
Operational Checking Account (Cuenta Corriente) with restricted cross-border payment functionality

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. Offshore electronic money institutions and neo-banks (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Mercury) are not licensed as banking institutions in Colombia and may not provide the mandatory foreign exchange intermediation or DCC reporting required for transactions above the regulatory threshold. These entities can only provide ancillary inbound/outbound transfer services through a locally licensed payment company (authorized by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia), but they cannot replace the domestic bank account required for trade finance and FDI registration. Any routing of export proceeds through an offshore EMI without an AIM would breach Colombian foreign exchange law and trigger penalties with DIAN and Banco de la República.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one legal representative or authorized officer must complete an in-person or remote-notarized KYC interview before the account is activated. Colombian banks generally accept an initial digital onboarding with electronic signature and biometric verification, but the final interview, including UBO documentation for foreign shareholders, must be conducted with a compliance officer; this can be done remotely under the Superintendencia Financiera's risk-based approach. All corporate documents (certificate of existence, bylaws, board resolution, and financials) must be legalized or apostilled; if any document originates from a foreign jurisdiction, it must be translated into Spanish by a certified translator and formally legalized. A local power of attorney or an agent resident in Colombia is strongly recommended to facilitate prompt approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore corporate ownership with opaque ultimate beneficial ownership or multiple intermediate holding companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate registry extract, notarized own-certification of the SAS's commercial structure, apostilled share register, up-to-date UBO declaration listing all natural persons with economic interest, passport copies, audited financial statements, and a clear business plan for the Colombian import/export operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction velocity in first 90 days and counterparties domiciled in jurisdictions outside the coffee origin country without a justified trade pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed sales and purchase contracts, proforma invoices, container shipping schedule, B/L and airway bills, SGS or Intertek quality inspection certificates, phytosanitary certificates, country-of-origin certificates, cargo insurance, and a reconciliation report showing the sourcing and selling margin in the Colombian entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire instructions routed to a private individual or an unregulated intermediary for payment of green coffee purchases.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contract naming the beneficiary, broker or agent agreement, invoice trail, evidence that the underlying coffee is physically transiting through the specified ports, and a DIAN export/import declaration reference number. All exceptions must be supported by a risk-mitigation memo approved by the bank's compliance unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of economic substance in Colombia or mismatch between declared objective and bank account usage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for a commercial office, employment contracts or payroll records of local staff, corporate tax filings (RUT, ICA, VAT), prior-period financial statements, and a 12-month treasury forecast demonstrating that the account is used exclusively for permitted coffee trade operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder must transmit a SWIFT wire in COP optionally converted at the bank's bid rate, or in USD, EUR, GBP, or another convertible currency through a correspondent bank to the AIM (e.g., Bancolombia or Banco de Bogotá). The wire instruction must reference: the CO_SAS name, tax ID (NIT), the exact purpose code 'Inversión Internacional – Capital de Empresas' (DCC code 10), and the beneficiary account number. The AIM will report the transaction to Banco de la República on the investor's behalf; the SAS must file the DCC Formulario 10 (Inversión Internacional) within the statutory window (generally thirty calendar days from receipt) and maintain the registration certificate for future profit remittance and liquidation. There is no mandatory capital escrow, but the funds must be registered as paid-in capital in the equity books and not used to finance related-party current accounts without a separate FX declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are Swift Wire (MT103) and Documentary Letters of Credit (UCP600). For MT103 settlements, the Colombian bank will debit the SAS's local COP account or the seller's USD account, converting at the TRM, and the payment instruction must include: contract reference, invoice number, country-of-origin certificate, and DIAN import declaration number when the transaction is simultaneous with customs clearance. For Documentary Letters of Credit, the CO bank issues an irrevocable LC for the green coffee shipment against prescribed documents including proforma invoice, phytosanitary certificate, certificate of origin, and B/L; the LC can be financed under a pre-import loan (prefinanciación de importaciones) using the coffee inventory as collateral. Settlement outside these clearing rails, including cash-in-advance paid to a non-bank, is only permissible for amounts below the regulatory threshold and must still be disclosed in the corresponding foreign currency declaration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Colombian Peso / USD Forwards (forwards del mercado cambiario) executed on trading platforms approved by Banco de la República with authorized financial institutions
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on the COP/USD TRM, cash-settled against the representative market rate, subject to evidence of underlying commercial exposure
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (COP/USD) used for long-term green coffee procurement and inventory financing, requiring a bank-approved hedging policy and underlying contract assessment
Foreign-Currency Options (puts and calls) on COP/USD, permissible only when used for hedging non-speculative trade flows and cleared through an authorized local broker or bank
FX Swap (Spot/Forward) transactions for short-term liquidity management between COP and USD, limited to the same-day and forward leg covered by the underlying trade payment schedule

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovation of the Commercial Registry (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil) via the Single Business and Social Registry (RUES)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (electronic submission through the RUES platform)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March of the calendar year following each 31-December fiscal year; the law fixes one single national deadline and does not use the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal surcharges of 5% (April), 10% (May–June) and 15% (July onward) of the renewal tariff; three consecutive years of non-renewal expose the registration to administrative cancellation, and foreign-trade authorisations, banking credit access and the issuance of the certificate of legal existence remain blocked until regularised

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Shareholders' Meeting and notarially certified minutes approving the annual financial statements and profit-allocation proposal (Acta de Asamblea Ordinaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate minutes book; certified copy lodged with the Cámara de Comercio when the minutes evidence third-party-relevant appointments or capital movements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March of the following year, i.e., within three (3) months after the 31-December balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors and the legal representative are jointly liable for damages caused by non-approval; the Superintendencia de Sociedades may order the meeting to be convened and may impose administrative fines on the incumbent officers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of the annual general-purpose financial statements (Estados Financieros de Propósito General) with the corresponding supporting notes and statutory certifications
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social — registry of commercial documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May of the following year; the shareholders' approval meeting must have taken place by 31 March, with the deposit effective under the permanent May window confirmed by Decree 2261 of 2023
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The commercial registry renewal cannot be completed without the deposit; the certificate of existence is issued with a note of the omission, blocking banking, customs and foreign-trade procedures; the Superintendencia de Sociedades may fine recalcitrant entities up to 20 monthly minimum wages (SMMLV)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update of the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF) — the mandatory ultimate-beneficial-owner declaration for the 31-December ownership position
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 June of the year following the fiscal year, within the annual window fixed by DIAN resolution; any mid-year share transfer or change in control requires an event-driven update within the shortened period set by DIAN (generally 15 business days)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: DIAN penalties under Article 651 of the Tax Code (up to 1% of gross income or 5% of equity, whichever is higher, capped per SMMLV); an inconsistent RUBF blocks issuance of tax-compliance certificates, commercial registry renewals and clearance of documentary credit operations with foreign banks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax and complementary return (Declaración de Renta y Complementario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Early-to-late April of the following year, assigned by the last digit of the NIT under the annual DIAN resolution (for income year 2024, filings were calendared 9–23 April 2025)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine of 10% of the tax due for the first month and 5% for each additional month or fraction (Article 641 E.T.), plus monthly default interest of approximately 2.5% (Article 634 E.T.); RUT suspension and blocking of export/import authorisations persist until the return is accepted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual exogenous information return (Información Exógena) covering payments to domestic suppliers, coffee-grower cooperatives, freight agents and cross-border counterparties, including the ICA/withholding reconciliation file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May of the following year, NIT-digit calendar fixed by annual DIAN resolution (for tax year 2024, the filing window ran from 20 May to early June 2025)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine under Article 651 E.T. of up to 1% of gross income (or the prorated value of the transactions omitted); the filing is a precondition for the validity of input VAT credits and for any export-incentive or refund application

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Industry and Commerce Tax (ICA) annual declaration and complementary collection, where the social domicile applies the annual filing regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Secretaría de Hacienda del municipio del domicilio social (e.g., Bogotá, Medellín, Cartagena)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual deadline set by each municipal ordinance, generally falling between April and July of the following year; taxpayers exceeding municipal thresholds must switch to bimonthly accrual periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal default surcharge of 1.5% per month or fraction plus late-filing fines; absence of a paz y salvo certificate blocks renewal of operating licences, public procurement eligibility and bank credit facilities in the domicile municipality

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (SAS) is required to appoint a statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal, a registered public accountant accepted by the Central Accountants Board) only if either: (i) total gross assets at 31 December exceed 5,000 SMMLV (COP 7,117,500,000 in 2025, approximately USD 1.7 million); or (ii) gross income exceeds 3,000 SMMLV (COP 4,270,500,000 in 2025, approximately USD 1.0 million). Below these thresholds, no independent statutory audit is imposed by law unless required by the company by-laws, the Superintendencia de Sociedades, or an LC/banking covenant
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian GAAP under Decree 2420 of 2015 as amended (IFRS as endorsed by the CTCP): full IFRS (NIIF plenas) for Group 1 large or public-interest entities; IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para las PYMES) for Group 2, which is the ordinary classification of a mid-sized specialty-green-coffee importing SAS; simplified micro-entity framework for Group 3. Books must be kept in Spanish and expressed in Colombian pesos (COP) unless NIIF/NIC 21 authorises a different functional currency and DIAN has accepted such treatment

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The entire shareholding chain must be traced upward to the final natural persons in the RUBF and confirmed annually by 30 June for the 31-December ownership position, per the yearly DIAN resolution. Every share transfer in a SAS is perfected by private instrument and becomes opposable to the company and third parties only upon entry in the Shareholders' Register Book (Libro de Registro de Accionistas); in parallel, the RUBF must be updated within the event-driven window (generally 15 business days) after any transfer or control change. Capital increases, reductions and by-law amendments arising from transfers are additionally recorded with the Cámara de Comercio. The RUBF protocol also applies to indirect transfers of the SAS through foreign holding entities, consistent with the substance-over-form tracing rule
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro de Registro de Accionistas (Shareholders' Register Book reflecting every issue and transfer of shares with date, counterparty, and instrument reference)
Libro de Actas de Asamblea (minutes of ordinary and extraordinary shareholders' meetings)
Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva (board minutes, where a board exists by by-law or director resolution)
Libro de Registro de Asistentes a la Asamblea (attendance register, or equivalent electronic attendance evidence)
RUBF supporting file documenting the ultimate-beneficial-owner tracing of the whole coffee-import structure
Commercial file for each green-coffee consignment: documentary LC, bill of lading, phytosanitary/invoice dossier and the DIAN electronic-invoice XML archive

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 180 – 420 per year for a registered-office and legal-representation address service, or for the renewal of a commercial agent where the social domicile is subleased from an office-services provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,500 – 6,000 per year for the Revisor Fiscal engagement when the asset or revenue threshold is exceeded; 300 – 800 per year for a limited independent review or agreed-upon procedures when the company remains below the compulsory thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (capital gains and ordinary corporate income unified at 35% for tax year 2024; surcharge of 3% only for financial institutions — not applicable to ISIC 4631)
